mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the monthly CPIAUCSL inflation index above 0.3% triggers a preemptive equity risk premium as investors anticipate future rate hikes, driving positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 0.3% in the current month
failure_condition: Over a 12-month window, 20-day forward returns do not outperform a 5-day rolling average during inflation spikes (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly rise in PAYEMS labor cost index (>50k new jobs) coinciding with a falling UNRATE unemployment rate signals labor market strength, which elevates equity valuations and produces positive 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by >50k and UNRATE falls by >0.1% in the same month
failure_condition: Across 10 such labor market tightening episodes, 60-day forward returns are not statistically higher than during neutral labor conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A consecutive monthly decline in RSAFS industrial production exceeding 2% suggests weakening demand for manufactured goods, which, when combined with a rising HOUST retail sales index, predicts negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS falls >2% for two consecutive months and HOUST rises by >1% in the following month
failure_condition: In 5 such demand contraction-retail strength events, 20-day forward returns are not statistically worse than during neutral demand (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly drop in INDPRO manufacturing production index (<-2%) combined with a continued decline in GDPC1 personal consumption indicates supply-side weakness, which depresses equity valuations and yields negative 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >-2% and GDPC1 falls by >1% in the same month
failure_condition: During 8 supply contraction episodes, 5-day forward returns do not fall below the mean of neutral supply conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in FEDFUNDS rates without a corresponding rise in CPIAUCSL inflation predicts a forward discounting effect that produces positive S&P 500 60-day returns.
failure_condition: Over 10 such rate easing episodes, 60-day forward returns fail to beat the mean of pre-easing periods (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A one-time monthly spike in PAYEMS employment exceeding 80k accompanied by a sharp drop in UNRATE (<3.5%) creates a labor market surprise that temporarily boosts risk appetite and drives positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises by >80k and UNRATE falls by >0.5% in the same month
failure_condition: Across 4 such surprise episodes, 20-day forward returns do not exceed the average of neutral labor market conditions (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly decline in both INDPRO and GDPC1 (each >1%) for three consecutive months predicts a dual supply shock that lowers growth expectations and produces negative 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >1% and GDPC1 falls >1% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: In 6 such multi-sector contraction episodes, 20-day forward returns do not underperform the mean of neutral supply (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden, one-time increase in FEDFUNDS above 5.25% in a non-inflationary month creates a risk-off reaction that drives negative 5-day S&P 500 forward returns as investors anticipate tighter policy.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises by >0.25% in a month with CPIAUCSL < 0.2%
failure_condition: During 3 such events, 5-day forward returns do not fall below the mean of pre-hike periods (t-test p > 0.05).
